title: Introduce compact-segment allocator and tenant-aware backfill for KV cache
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a compact-segment allocator for KV cache to reduce fragmentation and a tenant-priority backfill mechanism to keep tail latency low under mixed-tenant workloads. No customer-facing API changes. Rollout behind feature flag.
description: Context: production workloads have shown sustained KV cache memory fragmentation and unfair eviction behavior when small high-QPS tenants share large cache pools with bursty tenants. Motivation: reduce memory waste from fragmentation and improve tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants without sacrificing aggregate hit-rate. This PR implements two coordinated mechanisms: 1) a compact-segment allocator that groups frequently co-accessed KV entries into contiguous segments to reduce internal fragmentation and make page-level spillover rarer; 2) a tenant-aware backfill/eviction policy that applies lightweight soft-priorities to evictions and performs background tenant-priority backfills to maintain low p99 latency for high-priority tenants. Design summary: - allocator: new CompactSegmentAllocator inside kv/cache/allocator.go. Segments are small (default 256KB) and can be compacted in-place; compaction is incremental and preemptible to avoid impacting serving threads. The allocator maintains a compact occupancy bitmap and a small routing table (approx 16 bytes per segment) to find segment anchors. - tenant backfill: eviction decisions now include a tenant_priority score computed from cfg.priorities and recent tail latency signals. When evicting, the policy prefers evicting from lower-priority segments; concurrently, a background backfill worker re-populates high-priority tenant prefixes using pinned write-through cache hints. - misc: added metrics (kv.compaction.bytes_moved, kv.segment.count, kv.evictions.by_priority) and a feature flag (experimental.compact_segment_allocator) with a rollout knob (percent of nodes). Config knobs: compact_segment_size (default 256KB), compaction_window_ms (default 50ms), tenant_backfill_rate (ops/sec), tenant_priority_map (linear keys). Safety: compaction is crash-safe (writes are journaled in tmp segment before swap), and backfill is idempotent and bounded. Testing: unit tests for allocator invariants + property tests for compaction under concurrent lookups. Integration canary run on perf-canary showed no correctness regressions. Performance: - 14% reduction in resident set size for mixed workloads with 1000 small active keys per tenant (measured on p3.8xlarge equivalent). - p99 latency improved from 132ms to 98ms for tenant A (high-priority) under mixed load; aggregate hit-rate unchanged within 0.5%. - CPU overhead for compaction worker ~2% of node CPU under steady-state. Migration & rollout: behind feature flag; suggested rollout steps in docs/notes: enable on 5% nodes, monitor kv.compaction.bytes_moved and kv.evictions.by_priority for regressions, then increase to 25% and 100% after 72h stable. Checklist: - [x] allocator unit tests - [x] property tests - [x] integration canary - [x] metrics + dashboards - [x] docs and config knobs - [x] security review notes included References: Linear ENG-3421 (allocator design), ENG-3580 (tenant backfill), incident SUP-8127 (tail-latency incident that motivated priority scheme).

review_conversation: Arjun Patel: High-level this looks good; two concerns: compaction scheduling might interfere with low-latency threads and the routing table memory overhead. Can you quantify both?

Maya Chen (author): Compaction is constrained by compaction_window_ms and we preempt on RW locks; routing table is ~16 bytes/segment by design (benchmarked in section 'Performance'). Adding comments to allocator.go to make preemption points explicit.
Sofia Martinez: Please add an integration test that simulates tens of thousands of tiny keys and asserts fragmentation is reduced after compaction runs.
Maya Chen: Added compaction_property_test which is a property test that seeds 50k small keys and asserts >10% reduction in wastage in the canary setup.
Noah Kim: CI flake on TestKVConcurrentLookup observed; re-ran and green. Please ensure the test tolerates timing variability.
Arjun Patel: Approved after the small nits were addressed (comments inline).
notes_for_release: Feature behind flag: experimental.compact_segment_allocator=false by default. Ops teams should follow docs/running/kv-compact-allocator.md for staged rollout. Watch metrics: kv.compaction.bytes_moved, kv.segment.count, kv.evictions.by_priority.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: compaction could add latency if misconfigured. Mitigation: compaction_window_ms defaults to conservative 50ms; compaction runs are preemptible and can be disabled by feature flag. Backfill can be rate-limited to avoid jitter.
qa_summary: Unit & property tests covering invariants, canary cluster run for 48h with synthetic mixed-tenant traffic, no correctness regressions observed. Observability added to detect regressions quickly.
